name: Black conservatism in the United States
summary: Black conservatism is the strand of American conservatism within the African American community. It stresses self-reliance, personal responsibility, family, religion, patriotism, the Constitution and free markets over institutional explanations of racial disparities, and is skeptical of the welfare state and racial preferences.
scope: Mainstream modern Black conservatism as represented by Thomas Sowell, Walter Williams and Clarence Thomas, with Booker T. Washington's self-help philosophy as the historic precursor. Black Republican officeholders and commentators with differing emphases (libertarian versus social conservative) are not separately profiled.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free-market economists in this strand like Sowell and Williams oppose expanding state provision, but none of my sources address healthcare directly; inferred from their anti-welfare-state stance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Walter Williams argued minimum-wage laws discriminate against minority youth and subsidize racial preference, and Sowell's early Puerto Rico minimum-wage work moved him toward markets.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sowell and Williams are free-market economists, and the movement is described as emphasizing capitalism and free markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Support for capitalism and free markets makes public ownership of major industries foreign to this tradition; inferred from stated pro-market commitments.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from pro-capitalist, limited-government commitments, though Black conservatives rarely make tax rates a signature issue.

unions-good.rationale: Williams attacked laws such as Davis-Bacon for harming Black construction workers, implying hostility to union-backed protections; no source states a general union position.

property-fundamental.rationale: Washington stressed property ownership as the base of progress, and the movement stresses capitalism and the Constitution; inferred strong property emphasis.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Williams criticized occupational licensing and regulation as protecting incumbents at consumers' expense, so adherents oppose tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Williams reserved his fiercest criticism for the welfare state, arguing it subsidized poverty and damaged Black families; the movement stresses self-reliance over dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from capitalist and free-market commitments.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents are split between security-minded conservatives and civil-liberties-minded ones; sources are silent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Libertarian-leaning figures such as Williams and Sowell lean toward legalization while social conservatives and clergy oppose; Thomas dissented in Raich for limited federal power. Genuinely split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on individual liberty and constitutional originalism and skepticism toward racial grievance politics.

strong-leader.rationale: Not addressed; originalist, constitutionalist outlook favors limits on executive power, though some adherents back Trump.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement values the Constitution and limited government rather than abolishing the state; Sowell calls himself best labeled libertarian but disagrees with that movement on national defense.

limit-guns.rationale: Black conservative gun-rights voices are quoted saying gun control is about people control, and Thomas wrote the majority in Bruen affirming an individual right.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law-and-order emphasis is common, but the sources do not state a position on funding; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social conservatism and traditionalism suggest opposition; not addressed directly.

decide-locally.rationale: Thomas treats federalism as a foundational limit on federal power, and Washington favored local self-help; contested on civil-rights matters.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between tough-on-crime and rehabilitation themes.

traditional-family.rationale: Social conservatism and traditionalism are central, and Williams blamed welfare for damaging Black family structure.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social conservatism and the Christian-right association suggest opposition, but sources cite only individual anecdotes and attitudes are shifting.

abortion-legal.rationale: Thomas criticized Roe and joined Dobbs, and Black pro-life activists such as Mildred Jefferson are part of the movement.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement is tied to Christianity and the Christian right (T.W. Shannon: capitalism, Constitution, Christianity).

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents stress personal responsibility over institutional racism and oppose affirmative action; they do not usually endorse state remedies for past injustice, though they acknowledge past wrongs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Social conservatism implies rejection; not addressed directly.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Patriotism and traditionalism are named features of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: Washington favored gradual progress built on property, intelligence and character, and Sowell criticizes judicial activism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents split between pro-market openness and concern for Black workers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Patriotic, constitutionalist orientation suggests skepticism; not addressed directly.

free-trade.rationale: Pro-market economics suggests support, but no source states trade positions.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotism is a named feature; inferred, not stated on global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sowell dissents from militancy in foreign policy while others are hawkish; not addressed.

open-borders.rationale: Patriotism and rule-of-law emphasis imply rejection, though libertarian-leaning members differ; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Pro-capitalist growth emphasis is incompatible with limiting growth; inferred from stated free-market commitment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from skepticism of government intervention.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed by sources; no clear shared position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Pro-market, pro-energy outlook suggests mild support; not addressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Washington counseled gradualism and restraint and the movement is constitutionalist; revolution not addressed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sowell is famously critical of intellectual elites and judicial activism; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Williams and Sowell argue state direction lowers welfare and harms minorities; central planning is the opposite of their free-market doctrine.

socialized-markets.rationale: Capitalism with private ownership is preferred; not specifically addressed.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source addresses it; no adherent consensus.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from property emphasis and pro-capitalism; not addressed directly.

basic-income.rationale: Anti-welfare and self-reliance emphasis implies opposition; not directly addressed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Free-market orientation suggests opposition, though some adherents back Trump; not addressed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Williams criticized state-granted privileges and regulation; state investment direction conflicts with free-market doctrine.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Washington urged Black Americans to acquire property as the base of advancement; broad ownership fits that, though large corporations are not opposed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Capitalism is central to the movement; abolishing money and wage labor is contrary to it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; most adherents are not monetary radicals.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized wage and price setting contradicts free-market views of Williams and Sowell.

one-party-rule.rationale: Constitutionalism and democratic participation are central; one-party rule is rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: American constitutional patriotism makes this foreign; not addressed directly.

democracy-best.rationale: Washington accepted universal suffrage in principle and the movement is constitutionalist, though skeptical of majoritarian overreach.

direct-votes.rationale: Constitutionalist, originalist outlook favors representative republic; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Contradicts capitalism and constitutional order the movement supports.

right-to-secede.rationale: Patriotism and Constitution emphasis; not addressed directly.

natural-rulers.rationale: Washington and the movement stress equal rights before the law; but some admiration of merit. Inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Washington counseled restraint; sources do not directly state a principle.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement is tied to the Christian right and Christianity; not directly addressed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Thomas invokes natural law and religion matters, but explicit scriptural law is not a standard position; split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Some libertarian-leaning members like Sowell would open it, but most oppose; not addressed.

military-superiority.rationale: Patriotism implied; Sowell dissents on militancy but mainstream supports strong defense.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement is American-patriotic and civic; Washington spoke of races "separate as the fingers yet one as the hand."

class-struggle-history.rationale: Adherents reject class-conflict framing in favor of capitalism and individual responsibility.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Williams and Sowell argue disparities do not show injustice and oppose outcome-oriented policies like affirmative action.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from property and constitutional emphasis.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Sowell doubts race-targeted remedies lift anyone from poverty; no source addresses colonial reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from American patriotism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Pro-capitalism and self-reliance imply approval of self-interest within the market; not stated.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Emphasis on personal responsibility and tradition conflicts with constitutionalist individual rights; split.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; pro-family orientation implies opposition.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pro-capitalist progress orientation rejects this; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; conservative gradualism cuts against disruption while markets favor innovation.

human-enhancement.rationale: Social conservatism implies caution; not addressed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from distrust of bureaucratic planning.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; no clear shared position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Traditionalism pulls toward yes, patriotic progress narrative toward no; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Sowell emphasizes empirical evidence on policy outcomes, e.g. minimum wage and affirmative action worldwide.

direct-action.rationale: Washington rejected agitation; modern adherents criticize protest politics. Not directly stated.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Williams and Sowell's market economics rest on specialization and exchange.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Opposed to welfare-state logic and free-market view that rewards follow work.

production-for-use.rationale: The overview says black conservatism emphasises capitalism and free markets, and T.W. Shannon names capitalism among the 'three C's' that made the country great; Sowell abandoned Marxism for free-market economics.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capitalism is celebrated; exploitation theory rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contradicts constitutionalism and capitalism central to the movement.

collective-farming.rationale: Washington urged individual property ownership; collectivization is opposed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Adherents defend capitalism as a source of prosperity.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian-leaning like Williams are sympathetic; most conservatives accept taxation. Split.

harm-principle.rationale: Libertarian economics but social conservatism; split on moral regulation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Adherents resist group-based remedies and favor colorblind individual treatment, as Williams and Sowell opposing preferences.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; Constitution and democratic participation emphasized.

positive-liberty.rationale: Free-market tradition emphasizes negative liberty and self-reliance over provision of means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Sowell and others criticize academia and media elites; not stated as a power claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Sowell and Williams attribute disparities to culture, incentives and policy, not genetics; Black conservatives reject genetic racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Constitutional republic with parties assumed; not addressed.

total-state.rationale: Opposed to state direction of life; limited government and free markets central.

national-rebirth.rationale: Patriotic but not radical-decadence rhetoric; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Sowell's skepticism of militancy.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Alien to constitutionalism central to the movement.

bound-labor.rationale: Washington, born a slave, advocated free labor and property ownership; bound labor is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Originalist and Sowell-style empirical outlook rejects claims that truth just reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: Thomas references natural law as a philosophical background to the Constitution; Christianity is central to the movement.

single-common-good.rationale: Natural-law strands incline yes while pluralist market thinkers incline no; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Conservative-evangelical alignment suggests support; not addressed in sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to US adherents, inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Opposed to worker control of firms; inferred from capitalism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Sowell wrote Charter Schools and Their Enemies and defends school alternatives against public-school interests; Williams's profile is silent, so this is inferred from the pro-market, anti-monopoly outlook.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Free-market economics suggests skepticism of stimulus, but not addressed directly.

economic-freedom.rationale: Williams's critique of licensing and minimum wage and Sowell's market view treat economic liberty as foundational to minority advancement.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; constitutional rule of law preferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Patriotism and liberal-nationalist outlook; not directly addressed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christianity is central to the movement, so reason alone as the only guide is rejected.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-welfare and patriotic positions.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Critiques of welfare dependency and emphasis on self-reliance imply work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: Washington urged cooperation between races and between capital and labor, and adherents reject class conflict.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatism suggests traditional roles yet legal differentiation is rejected by constitutional equality; split.

ban-interest.rationale: Support for capitalism and free markets implies accepting lending at interest; the sources do not discuss usury.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Washington sought equal justice and Black conservatives reject legal segregation; Washington accepted social separation but not legal classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not the adherents' view of state; constitutionalism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Patriotism and traditionalism suggest assimilationist view; Sowell writes on cultural capital. Not stated directly.

elite-replacement.rationale: Black conservatives broadly do not endorse replacement theory; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; US two-party tradition assumed.

national-mission.rationale: Patriotism but Sowell is skeptical of militancy; split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Social conservatives reject structural-oppression frameworks, as they stress personal responsibility over institutional racism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-establishment and skeptical of political and intellectual elites in Sowell's vein, but no source states this about politicians as such.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Pro-life, pro-family movement opposes eugenic policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to US adherents.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Sowell calls himself best labeled libertarian on economics but disagrees on defense; Williams opposed the welfare state; others accept more state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Black conservatives affirm equal worth and colorblindness.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality before the law is a core claim: Washington demanded equal and exact justice to both races, and modern adherents stress colorblindness.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Irrelevant to adherents; rejects socialism altogether.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Patriotism rejects framing the US as colonial project.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality before law fits; not addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious liberty and evangelical tradition oppose.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Irrelevant to the US tradition; markets and property.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion important but vouchers favored over state instruction; split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialism and a strengthened socialist state are rejected as contrary to capitalism and constitutionalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Opposed to ethnic expulsion; equal rights emphasis.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian-leaning accept; others accept just uses of force by state. Split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Market competition as engine; not stated for peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; split between liberty and order.

separated-powers.rationale: Thomas is the foremost originalist and defends federalism and structural constraints on power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed to revolutionary vanguards; constitutional order.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Adherents reject welfare-state priority, while favoring opportunity through markets.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Property ownership emphasis (Washington) suggests support; not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Williams criticized union-friendly laws; not directly addressed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sowell and Williams point to policy and culture, not population, as causes.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Sowell stresses cultural differences but adherents generally affirm colorblind integration; not stated.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Constitutional originalism opposes suspending protections; Thomas deferential on war powers in some cases.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Williams and Sowell oppose price controls as economists.

party-controls-media.rationale: A tradition built on limited government and constitutional liberty would oppose state control of media, though the sources do not discuss it.

party-commands-army.rationale: Thomas's originalism ties authority to the Constitution, which places the military under civilian constitutional command, not a party; the question is not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: US constitutional model has president commanding forces but legislature approves; not applicable.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Black churches are mostly Baptist and congregational; not addressed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Patriotism is a named feature of the movement, so adherents would not wish their own government's defeat in wartime.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Socially conservative but liberty-minded; not addressed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Constitutional tradition of term limits; Thomas defends state term limits in Term Limits.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Patriotic strong-defense view favors alliances though Sowell dissents on militancy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning landlords would override private property and markets, which black conservatives defend; home ownership is encouraged, but a ban on renting is not discussed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Strong gun-rights stance but professional army accepted; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Irrelevant to the US; no stance.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Sowell critiques intellectuals; Sowell and others criticize elite credentialed class; not stated precisely.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Sowell argues cultures differ in outcomes and some features hold groups back; adherents are self-critical about aspects of culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Conservative law-and-order tradition; no source states Black conservatives' position.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Social conservatives oppose school-based sex-ed on gender equality; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian right ties but mixed support among Black conservatives; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatism suggests yes; not addressed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Thomas and the movement accept birthright citizenship tradition; not directly addressed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Assimilation and colorblindness suggest opposition; not addressed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Christian right alignment suggests support; not addressed for minorities.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Property and contract emphasis; not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to economic transformation of property systems.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty and constitutionalism; economic freedom treated as complement not substitute.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sowell critical of foreign aid in general; not addressed in sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; US already has it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources give no position on how the president is chosen; adherents accept the existing US system and split on the Electoral College.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The sources do not address territorial concessions in peace deals; adherents are not united on the question, so neutral.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property treated as fundamental by Washington; common-good limits not stressed.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents call Soviet system socialist and reject it; not addressed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No source addresses annexation or occupation; the movement has no distinctive position, so neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Black conservatism draws on the Black church and Christian social conservatism, which implies resisting state control of clergy; the sources do not discuss it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not applicable to US presidential system.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: No source addresses secession by force; adherents' constitutional patriotism pulls one way and federalism the other, so neutral.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The question of autonomous regions joining larger states is outside the movement's concerns and no source addresses it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Alien to republican and Christian monotheistic tradition of the movement.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Free-market orientation suggests sympathy; not addressed in sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: Culture and upbringing stressed by Sowell, but personal responsibility stressed too; split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Thomas's originalism holds officials to the Constitution's text, which implies no ruler stands above the law; the idea of a sovereign above law is not discussed.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not addressed by any source and adherents have no shared view on making it a central civilizational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed directly; separated powers favored.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court custody rules are not addressed in the sources, and adherents' traditional-family outlook gives no clear lean.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Black conservatives reject socialism, so its internal Maoist doctrine has no support; the sources do not discuss it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property rights fundamental; Washington urged acquiring property through work.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not addressed in the sources and the movement has no shared position on them.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The tradition's defence of religious liberty implies opposing penalties for leaving a faith, though apostasy is not discussed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not American conservative position; liberty emphasis.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Colorblind integration favored; Washington accepted social separation but in common civic life.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Washington urged Black Americans to cast down their buckets where they are and seek rights in the US, and modern Black conservatives stress American patriotism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Sowell stresses culture, incentives and ideas; opposed to Marxism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Williams criticized state-granted monopolies such as licensing; antitrust itself disputed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Free-market logic suggests opposition to bailouts; not addressed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Originalist Thomas defends constitutional constraints on majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Colorblind, anti-preference position extends to quotas; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sowell's free-market economics implies rejecting a closed autarkic bloc; colonial blocs are not discussed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Free-market skeptic of regulation; not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sowell and Williams stress market prices and material rewards as what drives effort, which implies rejecting moral incentives as the main spur; the sources do not discuss the idea.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Washington's gradualism and the tradition's patriotism and constitutionalism imply rejecting revolutionary insurgency, which the sources do not discuss.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal rights before the law; not addressed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Williams and other Black conservatives are ardent critics of affirmative action, arguing it harms intended beneficiaries and breeds low expectations.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: this strand stresses patriotism and the American founding, but its writers also champion Black history, so support for a nation-centred curriculum is moderate.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: Sowell wrote critically of conquest and empire while crediting cultural advances; Williams and Thomas stress individual liberty, so most adherents would reject rule over others.

patriotic-education.rationale: The strand stresses patriotism, the Constitution and national loyalty, and Washington urged loyalty to country.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: free-market economists in this strand favour private banking under rule-based central banks and distrust state control of money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Black conservatives defend capitalism as the system that lifts people out of poverty.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: not a concern of this domestic American strand and no source states a view.

delink-world-market.rationale: Sowell and Williams strongly favour free trade and market integration as the path to prosperity.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The strand rejects Marxist class exploitation theory and holds that workers everywhere gain from markets.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Williams and some libertarian-leaning figures defended private freedom of association, while social conservatives and Thomas-style jurists are split; adherents are divided.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Thomas's originalism and natural-law approach treat the written Constitution and Bill of Rights as binding limits on majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the strand's stress on self-help and equal citizenship under existing law, not on voiding old settlements; not addressed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the strand's constitutional republicanism, which has no place for hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: Thomas's originalism favours majority rule within constitutional limits and gives no individual a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Thomas's natural-law reading of the Constitution, under which an unlawful ruler loses legitimacy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: originalists favour separated powers and constitutional limits, not unlimited legislative supremacy; the monarchy question does not arise.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from conservative Christian moral outlook; not addressed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from conservative and free-market views that accept humane use of animals; not addressed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Washington's autobiography urges the educated and prosperous to help raise those below them, and the strand stresses charity and community over state programmes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses civic duty, patriotism and working within the Constitution, not withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: the strand rejects structural explanations of disadvantage and is sceptical of critical theories of culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from its scepticism of structural-oppression theories; not addressed directly.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Sowell and Williams attack explanations of poverty that rest on exploitation and stress domestic institutions and incentives instead.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from Washington's insistence on equal citizenship and the Constitution's equal treatment of all citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: Genuinely indifferent: the strand is anti-communist but has no stated view on other countries' parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Washington's self-help philosophy and Sowell and Williams's free-market scepticism of aid support reliance on one's own efforts.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: the strand favours settled constitutional order and has no irredentist tradition.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from colour-blind equal citizenship, which rejects political leadership by ancestry; Thomas and Williams oppose racial preferences.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Genuinely indifferent: the strand is anti-communist but has no stated view on anti-fascism as a constitutional principle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the strand's anti-communism and Cold War conservatism, which condemned both regimes as tyrannies.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Washington's autobiography treats slavery as the central issue of the war, and the strand does not dispute this.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: Black conservatives are divided, and many accept removing monuments to Confederate figures; not addressed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the strand's stress on family and fatherhood, and Sowell's attention to male outcomes; not stated directly.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the strand's social conservatism and its equal-treatment principle; not addressed directly.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Thomas's natural-law universalism and the strand's patriotic attachment to American institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the strand's constitutionalism, which keeps the military under civilian control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: free-market economists in the strand favour voluntary exchange over state-mandated pay for household work.

filial-duty.rationale: The strand stresses family, religion and personal responsibility, from which a duty to parents is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Black conservatives stress limited government and merit, but they take no stated position on examination for office; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Sowell and Williams are free-market economists who prefer open markets, so state blocks on foreign buyers are inferred as disfavoured.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Social conservatives and libertarians in the strand differ on divorce law and no source addresses it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Constitutionalists such as Thomas favour the representative system under law, not instructed delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Free-market economists of the strand favour private provision over state systems; inferred from Williams on the welfare state.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Booker T. Washington made property ownership central to Black self-help, and the strand upholds capitalism and private property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutionalist conservatives accept legislative control of spending; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Black conservatives do not address a common official language and adherents are split; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Free-market economists generally favour open property markets; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Williams argues that wage laws and preferences, not neutral rules, produce discrimination, and the strand stresses personal choice over institutional explanations of disparity.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The strand defends capitalism and free markets, so a harm-of-consumption view is inferred as disfavoured.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No source addresses foreign insurgencies and adherents are split between libertarian and hawkish views.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Thomas's constitutionalism and limited-government orientation suggest opposition to forced intervention in allies; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Sowell and Williams argue that government favours of business come from state power, but they do not treat corporate lobbying as the main problem; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; free-market and patriotic strands pull in opposite directions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Free-market critics of the welfare state oppose subsidies, though family stress is valued; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the property-rights emphasis of Washington, Williams and Thomas, which favours free sale and opposes exclusion.

job-guarantee.rationale: Williams and Sowell oppose government employment programmes and the welfare state, favouring markets and self-reliance.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; conservative views on democracy promotion are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Thomas draws on natural law but the strand stresses law and order and constitutional duty; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; patriotic conservative opinion is divided between hawks and restrainers.

industrial-unions.rationale: Williams and Sowell criticise unions and Davis-Bacon rules as harmful to Black workers; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The strand stresses equal justice and the Constitution and rejects scapegoating minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Black conservatives stress marriage and family as the base of social stability.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from constitutionalism and limited-government scepticism of state secrecy.

local-production.rationale: Sowell and Williams champion free trade and market specialisation over localism; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The strand works through churches, families and Republican institutions rather than informal anti-organisational politics; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Originalist and constitutionalist views such as Thomas favour the Constitution as the supreme law; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The strand values Christianity but also the Constitution and a pluralist civic nation; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the movement's patriotism and equal-citizenship stress, which rejects ritual submission by states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from limited-government and federalist leanings, which favour local retention of revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: it defends private property throughout and rejects common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its free-market, patriotic stance, which treats communism as an adversary.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Walter Williams and Sowell support school choice and market provision within publicly funded schooling, favouring non-state providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on religion and the Black church as sources of moral strength.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Williams and Sowell argue that free markets and capitalism have lifted living standards, including for Black Americans.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its view that equality is reached through personal effort, law and the existing economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on family responsibility and scepticism of the welfare state.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses free exchange and has no language purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from Thomas's originalist respect for the rule of law and binding legal commitments.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: common-property cooperative communities conflict with its defence of private property and markets.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its civil-rights-era commitment to equal treatment and scepticism of state steering by ethnicity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: It champions capitalism, so the claim that neither capitalism nor communism is sound is rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Black conservatives emphasise individual rights over group land claims, but adherents are split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No part of the strand denies the Holocaust; the strand's patriotism and constitutionalism stand opposed, inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the strand's limited-government bent suggests opposition to criminalising private conduct, inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The strand stresses the Constitution and individual liberty, so suppressing opposition conflicts with it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The strand is religious but constitutionalist, so punishing blasphemy is inferred as opposed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; the free-market view is that exploitation harms the ruling country too, inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; a Muslim religious obligation is outside the strand, inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's constitutionalism rejects forced removal on religious-law grounds, inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; the strand favours market and family institutions over participatory structures, inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The strand rejects institutional and structural explanations of racial disparities in favour of self-reliance and personal responsibility.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the strand's social conservatism suggests opposition, though libertarian members dissent.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's religious and family emphasis suggests opposition, inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The strand sits on the right and rarely adopts the combine-both-sides framing, inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Free-market economists like Sowell and Williams reject the premise that capitalism alienates workers, inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the strand's patriotism and religion suggest scepticism, though views vary.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The strand is religious but stresses constitutional rather than divine authority, inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; religious-conservative leanings suggest opposition to such bans, inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The strand opposes regulatory expansion on markets, inferred from Williams and Sowell.

social-market-economy.rationale: Sowell and Williams criticise the welfare state and favour largely free markets, inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The strand stresses patriotism, so abolishing armed forces is rejected, inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Free-market thinkers accept unequal outcomes from incentives, inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no settled position.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Black conservatives are constitutionalists, and Thomas's originalism treats office as filled under the Constitution; not addressed directly, so inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from Sowell and Williams's free-market views, which favour profit-making competitive lending; the sources do not discuss mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Free-market figures support repaying debts on market terms, but sovereignty and anti-state views split adherents; inferred as split.

property-franchise.rationale: Washington favoured equal qualifications applied fairly and modern figures like Thomas treat voting as an equal right of citizens; wealth tests are not part of the movement's platform.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from its Christian, family and free-market emphasis; the sources do not address the thesis.

reification.rationale: Inferred from Sowell's defence of markets as coordinators of knowledge; this Marxist concept is not discussed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from Sowell and Williams's defence of private enterprise and market ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Thomas's originalism and natural-law jurisprudence stress fixed, publicly known law applied by regular courts.

racial-franchise.rationale: Washington sought equal justice and Thomas and others reject race-based classification, so race-limited voting is rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as split between those favouring existing institutions and others open to technology.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the movement's constitutionalism and Sowell's critique of unaccountable officials.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement is socially conservative and Christian but not documented as seeking legal limits on interfaith marriage; inferred from its stress on individual liberty.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Washington stressed cooperation with whites and the movement stresses individual merit and open commerce, so group boycotts by owners' religion are rejected.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Constitutionalist and free-market conservatives like Thomas and Sowell favour limited government and representative institutions, and distrust untested democratic experiments; sortition is not addressed, so inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The strand stresses church and traditional religious values, as in Washington's Up from Slavery and the sources' account of religion; reinterpretation is not discussed, so this is inferred as leaning toward preserving doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sowell and Williams defend unequal wealth as the product of productivity and see government power, not private wealth, as the main threat to liberty; inferred from their free-market writings.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Adherents are split between libertarian-leaning figures who accept it and religious social conservatives who resist; no source addresses it directly.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Religion is a pillar of this strand (Washington, Thomas) and a state atheism programme is the opposite of its limited-government and faith-friendly stance.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The strand is pro-law-enforcement and tough on crime, favouring order and personal responsibility; abolition runs against its core view of the state role.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its preference for individual rights and colour-blind equal treatment over group-based political representation.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Washington stressed self-help and community uplift, and Sowell and Williams criticise government welfare programmes as harming the families they target.

term-limits.rationale: Limited-government conservatives commonly favour term limits; none of the sources discuss it, so this is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: a conservative preference for established representative institutions over novel direct-democracy schemes; not addressed in sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not an issue this strand has addressed, and adherents give it no consistent priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Black conservatism has strong ties to the traditional Black church, many of whose denominations restrict some offices to men, but adherents vary; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Adherents differ between traditional views of male headship and egalitarian family norms; the sources do not address it.

missingStatements.text: Racial preferences in college admissions and hiring should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Williams and other Black conservatives are ardent critics of affirmative action, arguing it harms intended beneficiaries and breeds low expectations.

notes: Positions on drugs, immigration, foreign policy and the death penalty vary between libertarian and social-conservative strands; most such answers are low confidence because my sources did not state them.
